previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was admitted for evaluation of chest pain, abdominal distention, and bilateral lower extremity edema. Initial assessment ruled out cardiac ischemia with normal cardiac enzymes and a negative stress test. Chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal in origin. Abdominal imaging showed no ascites or complete bowel obstruction, with mild distention likely due to partial bowel slowing. He was volume overloaded, prompting an additional dose of Lasix, while maintaining his baseline diuretic regimen. His condition improved, and he was discharged home on unchanged medications with plans for outpatient follow-up in primary care and hepatology.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma

Need for prophylactic vaccination and inoculation against influenza
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ y.o male with hx of HCC and HCV cirrhosis s/p 
TACE + RFA on tranplant list presenting with vomiting of blood 
streak emesis, increased abdominal distension and mild abd pain 
most consistent with gastritis. 
 
# Abdominal Pain and vomiting:  His exam and labs are very 
reassuring. Symptoms sound most consistent with either 
gastroenteritis or with worsening gastritis leading to nausea 
and vomiting. Suspect he does have decreased PO as his Cr was up 
from baseline on admission. Since he has known portal 
gastropathy and GAVE, suspect any vomiting would be blood 
flecked in him, and Hct stable, so this history is less 
concerning. No PVT on RUQ U/S and no evidence of ascites. 
Unlikely SBO since BM day prior to admission, abdomen soft and 
no concern on KUB. Continued home PPI and simethicone. Patient 
was tolerating po without difficulty and ambulating without 
assistance throughout admission. Pain treated with acetaminophen 
and one low dose oxycodone 2.5mg.
 
# Recent ___:  Baseline Cr is 0.6-0.8 and his Cr is currently 
1.1 likely due to decreased po intake. On diuretics at home 
(furosemide and spironolactone).   

# HCV and EtOH cirrhosis with treated HCC:  Prior 
decompensations include ascites but no current ascites on exam 
or RUQ U/S (which is limted for eval of this). Mental status 
clear. No PVT on RUQ U/S. MELD is quite low with normal 
creatinine, bilirubin, and INR. Continued lactulose, rifaximin, 
nadolol, Spironolactone and continue home Lasix.

# ___ s/p TACE + RFA: Follows with Transplant Hepatology.
 
# Anemia/thrombocytopenia:  Currently at his baseline, and 
likely due to his liver disease.  Should be rechecked as 
outpatient.
